title: SLO Decomposition and Real‑World Error Budget Playbook
content:
Summary:
This playbook defines a pragmatic process for decomposing high-level service SLOs into component-level SLOs, allocating and operating real-world error budgets, and connecting that work to capacity planning, incident reviews, and automation. It was written for Redwood Inference services (hosted API, dedicated, private control plane) and applies to model-serving and control-plane teams.

Goals:
- Ensure SLOs reflect user experience (P95 latency, success rate, and quality guards) while providing clear operational actions when budgets are exhausted.
- Create repeatable, measurable error budget allocations for downstream components (runtime, routing, cache layer, network).
- Tie error-budget consumption to capacity and scaling decisions, runbook actions, and incident review artifacts.

Scope:
- Applies to all externally visible service SLOs in the Redwood API product surface (text generation, embeddings, chat endpoints).
- Not intended for non-customer-facing infra (CI/CD pipeline SLOs have separate governance).
